tasks.q: An energy company replaces meter readers with smart meters. Who are the stakeholders? Select all that apply.
opts: People in other countries with no connection to it
tasks.fb: Stakeholders are affected by the change, not merely near it.

tasks.q: Which group do students most often miss?
a: People affected without having chosen to use the system
tasks.fb: Neighbours, passers-by, and the people whose jobs change.

tasks.q: Is each impact of online shopping local, national or global?
items: Empty units on the high street
More delivery vans on residential roads
Retail jobs replaced by warehouse jobs
Tax rules changed for online sellers
tasks.fb: A full-mark answer usually reaches all three levels.

tasks.q: Why does the exam want more than local effects?
a: Because computing decisions ripple outwards, and the biggest effects are often furthest away
tasks.fb: The waste and the work usually end up somewhere else.

tasks.q: An energy supplier replaces yearly meter readings with smart meters that send usage over the internet. How is each stakeholder affected?
tasks.fb: Accurate bills and no home visits are real gains; lost jobs and constant usage data are real costs.
tasks.title: Smart meters: who is affected?

tasks.q: Which impact of smart meters is a privacy issue rather than a cost issue?
a: Usage data reveals when a household is at home, awake, or away
tasks.fb: Half-hourly readings are a diary of a household's day.

tasks.q: Which sentence states a trade-off properly?
a: Deliveries become cheaper and faster, but drivers lose work and residential streets carry more traffic
tasks.fb: Gain, cost, and who carries each.

tasks.q: A student writes eight disadvantages and no advantages. What will the examiner say?
a: The answer is one-sided, so it cannot reach the top marks
Smart meters are worth introducing, provided customers can see and delete their own usage data and a non-internet option remains
Smart meters have advantages and disadvantages
It depends on your point of view

tasks.q: Put the parts of a full-mark impact answer in order.
steps: Describe the impacts on each, with reasons
Weigh the benefits against the costs
State a conclusion and justify it
tasks.fb: Same shape every time, whatever the scenario.

tasks.q: A hospital replaces paper notes with tablets. How is each stakeholder affected?

stakeholders.name: Nurses learning a new system mid-shift
Patients if the system goes down

tasks.fb: Better records and instant access are the gains; training time, downtime risk and workload are the costs.

tasks.q: Which is a national-level impact of this change?
a: If it works, the approach is adopted across the health service, changing how records are shared
Patients see a screen instead of paper
tasks.fb: Local effects happen on the ward; national ones change policy.

tasks.q: Sensors are installed across a town, tracking traffic, air quality and parking. How is each stakeholder affected?

stakeholders.name: People with asthma in the town

tasks.fb: Cleaner air and easier parking against surveillance and lost jobs: that's the trade-off to write about.

tasks.q: Is each impact of the smart town local, national or global?
items: Residents' movements recorded on their own street
Parking attendants' jobs lost in the town
New rules needed on how long sensor data is kept
Servers processing the data run continuously
tasks.fb: Local, national and global, with a reason for each: that's the full-mark answer.

info.title: Stakeholder is a real job
info.text: Large projects employ people whose entire role is consulting the groups a change will affect.

info.title: Unintended effects
info.text: Ride-hailing apps cut waiting times and also changed congestion, taxi licensing and public transport use in ways nobody planned.

info.title: Smart meter rollout
info.text: Britain's smart meter programme is one of the largest technology rollouts ever attempted here, and it has had every impact in this lesson.

info.title: Who pays?
info.text: A common exam trick: the group that benefits and the group that pays are different. Say so.

info.title: Conditions score
info.text: Conclusions with a condition attached usually read as more thoughtful than a flat yes or no.

info.title: Try it on anything
info.text: The method works on any scenario: streaming, self-checkouts, AI marking, electric cars, school fingerprint systems.
